claims.text: Greg Lavecchia, CEO and co-founder of Bloom Nutrition, asserts that daily fitness practice is foundational to entrepreneurial sustainability: physical fitness produces health, health produces confidence, and confidence removes fear — creating a compounding advantage that allows an entrepreneur to remain in the game longer than competitors who neglect it.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
claims.speaker_term: fitness is one of the most important things that I do basically every day of the week
conditions: applies to founders entering high-stakes business environments (e.g., eight-figure deal negotiations)
claims.mechanism: Fitness produces health; health produces confidence; confidence is defined as the capacity to handle stress; stress-handling capacity translates directly into entrepreneurial performance and longevity in the game.

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia argues that half of entrepreneurship is simply being sustainable in the game — staying healthy and confident long enough to compound results — rather than optimizing any single performance variable.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
claims.speaker_term: half of entrepreneurship is just being sustainable in the game

numbers.axis: proportion of entrepreneurial success attributable to longevity vs. tactical skill

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia defines confidence as the ability to handle stress, not as an internal feeling of certainty — meaning confidence is measurable by behavior under pressure, not self-reported state.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
claims.speaker_term: Confidence to me is the ability to handle stress

claims.text: Greg Lavecchia contends that physical fitness removes a significant subset of the variables that could undermine an entrepreneur's performance — specifically confidence deficits and health-driven incapacity — before those variables become active problems.
claims.speaker: Greg Lavecchia
claims.speaker_term: if you're fit, you remove so many of the potential variables of confidence or health that could come across your plate as an entrepreneur
conditions: founders who maintain consistent daily fitness practice
claims.mechanism: Consistent fitness eliminates health and confidence risks preemptively, reducing the probability that they emerge as acute constraints during high-stakes entrepreneurial moments.
bounded_by: Does not claim fitness eliminates all entrepreneurial risks — only the subset attributable to health and confidence

examples.text: Greg Lavecchia recalls entering rooms as a 25-year-old to negotiate eight-figure deals. He maintained a fitness discipline during that period deliberately, reasoning that visibly taking care of his own body signaled to counterparties that he had the discipline to take care of a large business transaction. The fitness practice was a credibility instrument, not merely a personal health choice.

practices.text: Treat fitness as a non-negotiable daily practice throughout your entrepreneurship career, not as something to be scheduled when time allows.
